comments.body:
REQUIREMENT ADDED FOR THIS STORY (operator-approved decision taken on `brutal-dyable-lion` / e59d). Recording it here so it cannot be missed when this story's plan is written.

## The cutover must tolerate a no-extras install
Story e59d ships the Cloud Markdown↔ADF functions with **marklas (plus its transitive mistune) as a pinned OPTIONAL EXTRA, lazily imported inside the three function bodies, with `ImportError` routed to the existing plain-text `adf.py` fallback.** It is NOT vendored.

Why the constraint exists: a review BLOCKED the original vendor-under-`src/rebar/_vendor/marklas/` plan because marklas needs mistune while the reconciler engine importing `adf.py` is contractually dependency-free (`pyproject.toml:69` — engine assets are stdlib-only package data; core `dependencies` stay pyyaml/jsonschema/referencing), and `src/rebar/_vendor/` is not importable from the reconciler subprocess. The lazy-import extra is the only option preserving that contract, and it mirrors the `agents`/`metrics`/`grounding` precedents.

**Consequence this story owns:** in an install without the extra, `adf.markdown_to_adf` / `adf_to_markdown` / `fit_markdown_to_adf_limit` return their PLAIN `adf.py` results. So the cutover — which repoints `AdfCodec`'s four ops and the live Cloud send/fit/compare sites — must behave correctly when the Markdown-aware path is silently unavailable, i.e. it degrades to today's plain-text ADF behaviour rather than raising or emitting a half-converted wire. That is the same plain path the flag-off rollback already targets, so it should fold into the existing rollback AC rather than adding a new mechanism.

Suggested AC to carry into the rewritten plan:
- [ ] With the marklas extra absent, the cutover path emits the plain-text ADF wire (today's behaviour) and raises nothing; verified by a test simulating the ImportError with the cutover flag ON.

## Two engine defects e59d measured that this story inherits
- **Combined-mark 2-cycle:** `A **~~both~~** end` ⇄ `A ~~**both**~~ end` alternates forever under repeated round-trip (exact 2-cycle). e59d adds a mark-order canonicalizer; the convergence proof this story needs depends on it.
- **HTML comments are dropped by marklas** (`text <!-- x --> more` → `text  more`; a lone marker → empty string). rebar's own `<!-- rebar:reconciler-echo -->` is an HTML comment, so any echo-suppression logic keying on that marker must not assume it survives a Markdown-aware encode. e59d mitigates by self-verifying and falling back to the plain encode for affected bodies.

## Unrelated blocker to fix when this plan is rewritten
This description is currently **21,954 characters**, well over the 8,000-character plan-review limit (gate P4, oversize), so `review-plan` cannot pass as written regardless of content. It needs to be cut down — the same rewrite that folds in the requirement above.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
SUCCESSOR SESSION — change 4 of 4 built (the `rich_sha` / `rich_reemit` persistence pair). Recording the design and the two constraints that shaped it, because neither is obvious from the plan text.

## What landed in the working tree
- `peer_state.rich_sha(wire)` — 16 hex chars (8 bytes). Shape-tolerant: Cloud's wire is an ADF *dict*, DC's a wiki *string*, so a non-string is JSON-serialized with sorted keys first. Without that, a re-encode emitting the same document with reordered keys would read as a changed body and reset the counter — masking exactly the loop this state exists to detect.
- `peer_state.note_rich_emit(entry, wire) -> int` — returns how many times in a row the SAME wire has been pushed. Change-gated both ways: `rich_sha` is written only when the wire actually differs, and a differing wire RESETS the counter, so an edited body never inherits the previous body's history. Zero is stored as ABSENCE, so a converging body adds nothing at all.
- `peer_state.RICH_REEMIT_OBSERVE_AT = 2` — an EQUALITY threshold, not a floor, so a divergence episode costs exactly one GET however long it lasts.
- `_clear_rich_reemit_on_body_refresh` wired into BOTH `set_baseline` and `merge_baseline`, gated on the DESCRIPTION value alone. A baseline write driven by status/assignee says nothing about the body; clearing on it would let a body loop forever while an unrelated field churned beside it.
- `apply_handlers._observe_rich_reemit` — at the threshold, ONE `get_issue_by_rest` read-back, overlaid into `ctx.synced_fields`. **It never writes a baseline.** The observed value reaches the baseline only through `reconcile._advance_baselines` -> `binding_store.merge_baseline`, so `_advance_baselines` REMAINS the sole baseline writer. A test drives the real `_advance_baselines` to prove the route, not just the value.

## Constraint 1 — binding_store.py is at 798/800 LOC
The obvious shape (thin `BindingStore` delegates, mirroring `get_baseline`/`set_baseline`/`merge_baseline`) is UNAVAILABLE: two delegates would put the file over the absolute module-size cap, and the limit is locked. So the new functions take the LIVE binding ENTRY rather than the bindings mapping, and the caller obtains it via `all_bindings()` — which copies only the OUTER mapping, so an in-place entry mutation is persisted by the store's own `save()`. That reliance is implicit, so it is pinned by `test_an_entry_mutation_survives_the_store_save_reload_round_trip` rather than left to a comment. Whoever later splits binding_store.py along a call-graph seam should reinstate the delegates.

## Constraint 2 — the post-push GET has no home in reconcile.py
The plan's phrasing suggested handing the observation to `_advance_baselines`, which lives beside `reconcile.py:600`. There is NO transport in scope there — `grep -n client src/.../reconcile.py` returns nothing; the transport is resolved in the applier. So the read-back is in `handle_update`, which already holds `ctx.client` AND `ctx.binding_store`, and it reaches the baseline as a `synced_fields` overlay — the same channel bug e6e9 built for confirmed writes. The sole-writer invariant is satisfied by the ROUTE, not by co-location.

## Flag gating (deliberate, and a judgement call worth review)
The whole mechanism is skipped unless `rich_text.cutover_clients()` is non-empty, resolved by a function-LOCAL import (core apply path must not take an import-time dependency on the adapter layer) and read at call time, failing closed exactly as story 1710's resolver does. With the flag off — the default — there is no digest, no counter and no GET, so the plain-wire path is byte-identical to before the cutover shipped. The alternative (apply the loop-bound universally) would have been a user-visible sync-semantics change beyond this story's scope.

## Evidence
15 new tests in `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/state/test_rich_reemit_state.py`; mutation-checked (forcing the threshold to 99 fails 3 of them, so they are load-bearing rather than vacuous). `make lint` + `make typecheck` clean; 10 `check_*` gates OK; complexity baseline active=53 new=0 increased=0; module-size contract passes (apply_handlers 531, peer_state 269).

Gerrit 1716 (change 3, tests-only) is at LLM-Review +1 with CI still running; this change stacks on it.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
CHANGE 4 PUSHED — Gerrit **1720** `Bound a looping rich-text body with one GET` (commit 4962e18789), the last of this story's four changes. Two things the local gates caught that are worth carrying forward.

## The adapter-layer gate I first wrote was ILLEGAL, and two tests said so
My first cut resolved the cutover flag with a function-LOCAL import of `adapters.jira_family.rich_text.cutover_clients` from `apply_handlers`, on the theory that a call-time import avoids the layering problem. It does not — `test_backend_neutrality.py::test_scalar_core_imports_no_jira_adapter[apply_handlers.py]` and `test_jira_family_boundary_heldout.py` both fail on it, because they scan for the SYMBOL, not for import-time binding. Core may not reach into the vendor package at all; the direction is one-way.

The repo already documents the sanctioned alternative, in `config.local_to_jira_status`'s comment: keep a SECOND independent read and pin the two together with a PARITY TEST, rather than an import that inverts the layering. So `_rich_cutover_active()` now reads `rebar.config` directly (the lazy read a dozen core modules already use), fails closed on `ImportError`/`ConfigError`, and is pinned against `cutover_clients()` across all five flag values including the unparseable one. Anyone wiring another core site to this flag should copy that shape, not the import.

## `docs/env-vars.md` is GENERATED and cites LINE NUMBERS
Adding one import line to `apply_handlers.py` shifted a cited line from `:63` to `:64`, so the env-var registry drift gate would have failed CI on a change that touches no env var at all. Regenerated with `python scripts/gen_env_registry.py` and committed. Any change that moves a line in a file containing a non-literal `os.environ.get` needs that regeneration — worth checking before push rather than after a `Verified -1`.

## Gate results at push
- `make lint` + `make typecheck` clean; complexity baseline active=53 new=0 increased=0; module-size contract passes.
- 10 `check_*` gates OK; all four generators (ADR index, prompt index, env registry, CLI/MCP reference) no-diff apart from the env registry above.
- CI-equivalent suite: **12721 passed, 0 failed**. 23 `leaked new entries into REPO_ROOT` teardown ERRORs were self-inflicted — an `rebar review-plan` run concurrently in the same worktree emits sidecars under the repo root, which the leak guard sees. Re-running the affected files in isolation: 73 passed. Lesson: do not run an LLM op inside the worktree a suite is running in.
- `tests/integration`: 194 passed, 1 skipped (same self-inflicted leak errors, same cause).

## AC status
The final AC — inline change-gated 8-byte `rich_sha`, no per-pass timestamp, zero entries changed on a no-op pass — is covered by `test_a_pass_that_pushes_no_description_changes_zero_entries` (asserted on the bytes the store would commit) and `test_the_state_pair_costs_well_under_the_per_version_budget`. NOTE for the record: the AC names a "git-delta cost harness" verifying ≤0.07 KB/version; **no such harness exists anywhere in the repo** (searched `tests/` and `scripts/`). It is realized here as a direct byte-level assertion on the serialized per-binding delta, which measures the same quantity. Flagging rather than silently reinterpreting.

Remaining before close: 1716 and 1720 both green and submitted.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
AC AUDIT before closing — and it found a REAL GAP, so this story gets a fifth change (Gerrit **1728**).

I checked every test this story's ACs name against merged `main` rather than assuming the landed changes covered them. Three names did not exist:

| AC names | actually landed as |
|---|---|
| `test_cloud_cutover_converges` | `test_cloud_cutover_sends_structured_adf` + `test_lossy_body_converges_across_passes` / `test_cutover_does_not_mass_rewrite_already_synced_bodies` |
| `test_dc_cutover_converges` | `test_dc_cutover_sends_rendered_wiki` + the same convergence pair |
| `test_dc_comment_diff_unchanged_by_cutover` | **nothing — genuinely absent** |

The first two are naming drift: the predecessor split each "posts once AND converges" AC into a send test and a convergence test, which is better decomposition, and both halves are covered. Not a gap.

The third was a real hole, and a consequential one. The cutover redefines `WikiTextCodec.normalize_outbound` to be derived from `to_wire`, so on DC it RENDERS instead of being the identity — and `outbound_comments._diff_comments` builds its LOCAL dedup key with exactly that operation. Had the cutover reached that seam, every already-mirrored comment's key would shift to its rendered form while Jira still holds plain text, so every comment would read as absent and **the differ would re-post the project's entire comment history** on the pass after an operator flipped a flag whose name says nothing about comments — unrecoverable from Jira's side.

It does NOT reach it: `_resolve_codec(None)` returns `_IdentityCodec` and no caller wires a real codec into the comment path (that is story `emersed-specific-mutt`'s job). So the AC's claim is TRUE — but it was true by construction and completely untested, which is the worst combination, because the change that would break it is a one-line wiring edit that looks obviously right.

1728 pins it from both ends: the resolver directly (so a regression names the seam that moved, not just the symptom) and the resulting diff asserted identical with the flag off and on, over a mixed case (one already-mirrored comment, one genuinely new) so a key that shifted but still emitted something is caught too. Plus a guards-the-guard test proving the rendered form actually differs from the raw one — without it the others could pass vacuously.

One test-authoring note worth carrying: the flag is driven through `REBAR_RECONCILER_RICH_TEXT_CUTOVER` rather than a stubbed config object. The comment differ resolves the vendor adapter AND its transport from the same config, so a stub carrying only `rich_text_cutover` raises `AttributeError: 'R' object has no attribute 'backend'` and then `'_Cfg' object has no attribute 'jira'` — failures that read like product defects. The env override exercises the real resolution path and needs no stub at all.

Landed so far: 1710, 1712, 1716, 1720. Outstanding: 1728.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
REVIEWER CAUGHT A REAL BUG IN LANDED CODE — not just a stale citation. Filing the detail here because the finding's value was in what it made me check, not in the wording it objected to.

The re-review BLOCKED on the plan claiming `adapters/jira_datacenter/_issues.py` had an `_DESCRIPTION_CODEC` that applied `fit_outbound` WITHOUT `to_wire`. That claim is stale — change 1710 already fixed that site (it is now `_description_codec()` composing `to_wire(fit_outbound(...))`). Correcting the sentence would have been the cheap response.

But the reviewer also stated, as part of refuting me, that **`backend.py`'s `_map_local_to_dc_fields` applies `fit_outbound` with no `to_wire`**. I checked, and it was TRUE:

```python
codec = WikiTextCodec(rich="dc" in cutover_clients())   # builds a RICH codec…
"description": codec.fit_outbound(ticket.get("description") or ""),  # …then never renders
```

That is a genuine defect in shipped code, inside this story's scope. `_map_local_to_dc_fields` is `map_ticket_to_remote`'s implementation — a DC create path entirely separate from `_issues._translate_create_fields`. With `rich_text_cutover = dc`, a NEWLY CREATED issue would carry raw Markdown while every later update carried rendered wiki: the issue looks like broken formatting until someone happens to edit it, and nothing in the suite would have said so.

**Why it survived four changes:** the plan warned about exactly this hazard ("TWO other DC send sites … BOTH must route through `to_wire`") and 1710 fixed ONE of the two. The test written to prove it — `test_dc_create_path_renders_like_the_update_path` — exercises `_issues.py` only, so it passed while its sibling stayed broken. A test named after the general property but bound to one of two implementations reads like coverage and is not.

**Fixed:** `_map_local_to_dc_fields` now composes `to_wire(fit_outbound(...))`, with two tests bound to THAT function by name — `test_dc_backend_create_path_renders_like_the_update_path` and `..._is_unchanged_when_flag_is_off` (the rollback must cover both paths too). Revert-checked: restoring the old line fails the new test with `'# Heading…' == 'h1. Heading…'`, so it is load-bearing.

The plan text is also corrected to describe both sites accurately rather than describing a pre-1710 state.

Lesson worth carrying past this epic: when a plan says "BOTH sites must X", the covering test must name the SITE, not the property. Two tests bound to two functions, not one test bound to whichever implementation the author happened to import.

compiled_state.description:
# Live rich-text cutover + state echo suppression + concurrency conflict safety

## Context / Problem
Cut the live Cloud and DC send paths to the rich codecs (needs `e59d`, `271c`).
DC's codec is lossy/one-way, so `decode(encode(x))==x` cannot gate loops; echo suppression is
by **state**: current Jira value vs last-synced baseline (ADR 0026;
`binding_store.get_baseline`/`set_baseline`; `_BASELINE_FIELDS` in `peer_state.py`).

**Reused unchanged:** the ADR-0026/d6bd baseline diff (`get_baseline` via `InboundMapper`,
`outbound_field_diff.py`; `description` in `_INBOUND_MIRRORED_FIELDS`, via
`_compute_field_changes`); once-only re-emit convergence needs the codec law
`normalize_outbound(t) == decode_inbound(to_wire(t))` (`test_rich_text_codec.py`, a32a) plus
round-trip idempotence. **The non-idempotent tail is bounded.** Consecutiveness is PERSISTED,
not inferred: the inline binding record carries a change-gated `rich_reemit` counter beside
`rich_sha`, incremented when a field is emitted with `rich_sha` unchanged and reset to 0 when
`rich_sha` changes or the baseline refreshes — so it stays 0 (no churn) on healthy bodies. At
`rich_reemit == RICH_REEMIT_OBSERVE_AT` do ONE post-push GET and overlay it via
`binding_store.merge_baseline`, so `_advance_baselines` REMAINS the sole baseline writer. The
GET lives in `apply_handlers.handle_update`. Comment dedup intact.

## The live cutover
- **Cloud:** point the four `AdfCodec` ops at `adf.py`'s Markdown-aware fns
  (`to_wire→markdown_to_adf`, `decode_inbound→adf_to_markdown`,
  `normalize_outbound→adf_to_markdown∘markdown_to_adf`, `fit_outbound→fit_markdown_to_adf_limit`)
  + whole-codec plain-text fallback; pin test `test_rich_text_codec.py:198/205/207/208`. Reroute:
  encode `adapters/jira/acli.py`, `acli_cli_ops.py`; fit `jira_fields.py`; compares
  `adf.normalize_description`/`adf.fit_text_to_adf_limit` (`outbound_fields.py`,
  `inbound_differ.py`) — **send-fit and compare-fit must be one transform**.
- **DC:** `WikiTextCodec.to_wire` delegates to `wiki_render.render_markdown_to_wiki` (`271c`);
  **redefine `WikiTextCodec.normalize_outbound` to `decode_inbound(to_wire(t))`**, restoring the
  codec law. Send composes `normalize_outbound(fit_outbound(value))` (`outbound_mapper.py`) →
  rendered wiki on `issue.update(fields=…)`. **TWO other DC send sites:**
  `_map_local_to_dc_fields` (`adapters/jira_datacenter/backend.py`) AND
  `_issues._translate_create_fields` (via `_description_codec()`) — BOTH must compose
  `to_wire(fit_outbound(...))` or they ship un-rendered Markdown on CREATE while updates ship
  rendered wiki. Retarget the DC pin tests.

## Design decisions
1. **Two DISTINCT compares — do not collapse.** *Emit (`outbound_field_diff.py:288`),
   local-vs-REMOTE — UNCHANGED:* `normalize_outbound(fit_outbound(local))` vs
   `canonical_remote["description"]` = `decode_inbound(remote_wire)`
   (`inbound_mapper.map_remote_to_local`); both decoded → lossy round-trip cancels; an
   un-normalized remote forces the one-time legacy re-emit (`outbound_fields.py:586`).
   *Baseline (`_suppressed_by_inbound` `:323`, `_local_matches_baseline` `:464`) — LOCAL side
   normalized:* raw local Markdown vs `decode(baseline_wire)` differ → "local changed" every
   pass; route the local side through `RichTextCodec.normalize_outbound` (`decode∘to_wire`, via
   `OutboundFieldMapper.map_fields_to_remote`), sole normalizer.
   `_remote_matches_baseline` (`:399`) — UNCHANGED.
2. **Concurrent both-sides edit — unchanged (a713 local-wins).** Both differing from
   `baseline` → `outbound_field_diff.py:450-457` appends `(jira_key, fname)` to
   `conflict_sink`; `run_differs.py:_emit_outbound_field_alerts` (`:97`) emits the deduped
   alert. Emit stays local-wins; inbound description stays **additive**
   (`conflict_resolver.FIELD_CLASSES`, `resolve_additive`).
3. **Shared-op side effect.** The redefinition also reaches the DC comment-diff dedup key
   (`outbound_comments._diff_comments` via `_resolve_codec`); that path keeps the
   identity/plain normalizer UNCHANGED.
4. **Origin-gating + churn.** Updates fire only when `local != baseline`, so a Jira-authored
   construct (panel/mention/date, decoded by `adf.py`) survives an edit-free pass.
   Store a change-gated `rich_sha = sha256(rendered_wire)[:16]` (8 bytes) **inline** in the
   binding (0.07 KB/version; a per-pass timestamp reproduced `0303`'s 12.62 KB anti-pattern);
   the compare never writes back.

## Scope (IN)
- `adapters/jira/rich_text_codec.py` (+ fallback), `adapters/jira_family/rich_text.py`, Cloud
  consumer sites above, `backend.py` (`:57`) CREATE path — gated.
- **Cutover flag (NEW config, defaults OFF):** `reconciler.rich_text_cutover`
  (`off`|`cloud`|`dc`|`both`) across the standard four-file surface (`_config_schema.py`,
  `_config_sources.py`, `tests/golden/config_surface.json`, `docs/config.md`). Gates both send
  paths; off = plain/identity wire (the rollback). Enable per client, Cloud then DC, after canary.
- `binding_store.py` inline `rich_sha`; `outbound_field_diff.py` (`:323`, `:464`) local-side normalize
  only (`:292`, `_apply_mutations` untouched); tests under `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/`.

## Scope (OUT)
- No new three-way merge, LWW clock, conflict sink or parallel `norm()`; no change to
  `FIELD_CLASSES`/`_field_contract` or `inbound_fields.normalize_rich_text`; comment
  rendering and the DC dedup-key migration (`789c`).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Cloud: a converted ADF description posts once; a second pass emits zero updates
  (`test_cloud_cutover_sends_structured_adf` + `test_lossy_body_converges_across_passes`).
- [x] DC: `issue.update(fields=…)` gets rendered wiki, not raw Markdown; a second pass emits
  zero updates (`test_dc_cutover_sends_rendered_wiki` +
  `test_cutover_does_not_mass_rewrite_already_synced_bodies`).
- [x] TWO distinct compares: emit on the plain inbound-decoded remote; baseline compares'
  LOCAL side through `normalize_outbound` to match `decode(baseline_wire)`; a no-edit body stays
  suppressed across passes, a rebar edit shows changed, a legacy body upgrades once then
  converges (`test_lossy_baseline_compare_local_normalized`, `test_legacy_body_upgrades_once`,
  `test_lossy_body_converges_across_passes`).
- [x] The `WikiTextCodec.normalize_outbound` redefinition leaves the DC comment-diff dedup key
  unshifted; comment-diff converges with no duplicate re-post
  (`test_diff_comments_cutover_neutral.py`, all 4 tests).
- [x] Outbound fires only on a rebar-originated change (`local != baseline`); the baseline
